request: Analyze GSE289569 for PMID 41118251 (A role for the transcriptional coregulator RIP140 in the control of muscle endurance fitness.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (Salmon/tximport, mm10) of EDL muscle, male mice, n=3 per group (FIG4 A; S4.12.p1; S4.13.p1)
final.inclusion: Male strNrip1-/- (MCK-Cre) and WT littermates, 8 wk voluntary wheel running vs sedentary from 8 wk of age; EDL from an independent cohort not subjected to additional testing; non-runners (<5 km/night) removed (S2.3.p1; S4.8.p1; S4.12.p1; S4.1.p1)
final.primary_estimand: Paper's primary transcriptomic estimand is the genotype effect (KO vs WT) within sedentary and within trained EDL (S2.4.p1, FIG4 B/D). For this request the exercise estimand is the training effect (Trained vs Sedentary) within WT, and within KO; the authors computed these Train-Sed|WT and Train-Sed|KO DESeq2 contrasts and deposited them in GEO but report no counts in the text.
planned_contrasts: Train vs Sed within WT (deposited GEO table column 'Train-Sed|WT'; not counted in the text)
Train vs Sed within KO (deposited 'Train-Sed|KO'; not counted in the text)
KO vs WT within Sed (S2.4.p1: 421 up / 288 down)
KO vs WT within Trained (S2.4.p1, FIG4B: 616 up / 506 down)
final.repeated_measure_unit: none (one EDL sample per mouse; independent groups)
final.paper_method: DESeq2 v1.44.0 on tximport gene-level counts, pairwise group comparisons (S4.13.p1-p2; GEO data_processing)

paper_threshold.source_locator: S4.13.p2 (FDR <= 0.05 and |FC| >= 1.2); S2.4.p1/FIG4 state FC > 1.2 and FDR < 0.05

paper_results.physiology: 2-way ANOVA: significant training and genotype effects on VO2max, no interaction (S2.3.p1)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S4.23.p1 names GSE289569 as the strNrip1-/- with training RNA-seq. S2.3.p1/S4.8.p1 define the 2x2 genotype x voluntary-wheel-training design; S4.13.p2 gives DESeq2 and FDR<=0.05, |FC|>=1.2. The text reports only KO-vs-WT DEG counts; the GEO supplementary table also carries the authors' DESeq2 Train-Sed|WT and Train-Sed|KO results, which define the exercise estimand the request asks for. Recomputing the deposited padj/log2FC at the paper threshold gives 421/288 and 616/506 exactly, so the deposited table is the authors' result.

checks: S4.23.p1 names GSE289569 as the strNrip1-/- training RNA-seq
GEO metadata: 12 EDL samples, Ctrl/Nrip1KO x Sedentary/Trained, 3 per cell, Mus musculus, matches FIG4A n=3 per group
supplementary matrix columns WT/KO x S/TR x EDL x rep1-3 = 12 samples
deposited DESeq2 columns reproduce the paper's 421/288 and 616/506 KO-vs-WT counts

ownership.reasoning: Paper, GEO series, and matrix agree on the 12-sample 2x2 EDL design; deposited author results reproduce the text's counts exactly.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns are the authors' labels (WT_S_EDL_1 ...). prep/prep_matrix.py renames them by decoding the label vocabulary (WT->Ctrl, KO->Nrip1KO, S->Sedentary, TR->Trained, replicate kept) to <genotype>_<training>_<rep>; key_patterns derives the same key from the GEO title. Exact match on that key, never by position. Derived formula-safe columns geno (WT/KO) and train (SED/TR).

final.source: GSE289569_fpkm_and_deseq2_results.tsv.gz (12 FPKM columns split out by prep_matrix.py)
final.paper_input: tximport gene-level counts from Salmon (S4.13.p1) - not deposited

matrix.reasoning: GEO data_processing: 'Tab-separated table with FPKM values for all samples and DESeq2-generated adjusted p-values and log2 fold changes'. Values are non-integer, non-negative in the sample columns, max ~2.4e5; consistent with FPKM. No raw or estimated counts are deposited (no _RAW.tar, sample supplementary files NONE).

final.analysis_type: factorial 2x2 (cell-means, one model on all 12 samples)

candidates.value: pool genotypes for Trained vs Sedentary
candidates.reason_rejected: genotype strongly changes expression (709-1122 DEGs); the authors analyse training within genotype
one model on all 12 samples shares the variance estimate; the authors' contrasts all come from the 4-group design

design.reasoning: S2.3.p1 / FIG4: 2x2 genotype x training, n=3 per cell, independent mice. The exercise question is Trained vs Sedentary within genotype; the KO-vs-WT contrasts are the paper's reported results and run as secondary from the same model. Interaction is exploratory (paper reports no transcriptomic interaction test).

covariance.reasoning: One EDL sample per mouse, independent groups; GEO records no batch, lane, or date variable; all males (S4.1.p1). No blocking unit.

final.method: limma (limma-trend on log2(FPKM+1), joint cell-means model)

paper_route.reason: only FPKM deposited; DESeq2 needs counts and FPKM cannot be converted back to counts

deviations: limma on log2(FPKM+1) instead of DESeq2 on counts; counts will differ from the authors' deposited DESeq2 results

method.reasoning: Matrix-method policy: FPKM goes to limma on a log scale. No extra expression filter: the deposited matrix already holds only 17,752 genes, each expressed in at least one sample.

final.deviation_note: Paper's FDR<=0.05 and |FC|>=1.2 (log2(1.2)=0.2630344) applied to limma BH-adjusted p and logFC.

threshold.reasoning: S4.13.p2: adjusted P (FDR) of 0.05 or less and absolute fold change of at least 1.2. The results text says FC > 1.2 and FDR < 0.05; on the deposited results both readings give identical counts.

caveats: exercise contrast counts are not stated in the paper text; their reference counts come from the authors' deposited DESeq2 table at the paper threshold
limma on FPKM vs authors' DESeq2 on counts

study.reasoning: KO-vs-WT counts from S2.4.p1 (421+288, 616+506). Train-vs-Sed reference counts (39 up/12 down WT; 73 up/55 down KO) recomputed from the authors' deposited DESeq2 padj/log2FC at the paper threshold. Named genes from S2.4.p5-p6 (NMJ and angiogenic genes up in KO EDL).

discrepancies.data: authors' DESeq2 Train-Sed|WT and Train-Sed|KO in the GEO supplementary table

executions.name: joint
executions.reasoning: One limma cell-means model on all 12 samples; planned exercise contrasts within genotype (primary WT), genotype contrasts as reported in the paper, interaction exploratory.

enrichment.reasoning: Pathway view of the exercise effect in WT EDL; the paper discusses training-induced oxidative/mitochondrial programs.
